module_title: Network Types (PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN) - Foundational Basics
introduction: A computer network is a group of two or more computing devices connected together to share resources (like printers or internet access) and data. In Tier-1 competitive exams, networks are primarily classified and tested based on their 'Geographical Coverage Area'.

core_concepts.title: PAN (Personal Area Network)
core_concepts.description:
The smallest type of network. It is organized around a single individual, typically within a range of 10 meters. 
Examples: Connecting wireless headphones via Bluetooth, or connecting a laptop to a smartphone's mobile hotspot.

core_concepts.title: LAN (Local Area Network)
core_concepts.description: A network that connects computers within a limited, small geographical area such as a single room, an office building, or a school campus. It is highly secure and offers very high data transfer speeds. (Examples: Ethernet cables, Office Wi-Fi).

core_concepts.title: MAN (Metropolitan Area Network)
core_concepts.description:
Larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN. It covers an entire geographical city or a large university campus. 
Examples: A city's local Cable TV network, or a network connecting different branches of a bank within the same city.

core_concepts.title: WAN (Wide Area Network)
core_concepts.description:
The largest type of network. It covers broad geographical distances, bridging across states, countries, or even continents using leased telecommunication lines or satellite links. 
Example: The 'Internet' is the world's largest public WAN.

important_entities.name: The Internet
important_entities.significance: Because the Internet spans the entire globe and connects millions of smaller LANs and MANs together, it strictly falls under the category of a WAN (Wide Area Network).

important_entities.name: WLAN (Wireless LAN)
important_entities.significance: When a Local Area Network uses high-frequency radio waves (Wi-Fi) instead of physical physical Ethernet cables to connect devices, it is called a WLAN.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The MAN vs. WAN Geographical Trap
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a question states a network connects computers across a 'City', the answer is strictly MAN. If the question states it connects branches across 'Different Cities' or 'Across the Country', the answer upgrades to WAN.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the size hierarchy from smallest to largest: PAN < LAN < MAN < WAN.

exam_strategy_tips: A guaranteed Tier-1 question format: 'Bluetooth technology is an example of which type of network?' Without hesitation, select PAN (Personal Area Network).
